items.title: Beyond tree cover: mapping the world’s forest types
items.description: A global map categorizing every 10-meter patch of land on Earth into distinct forest types.
items.excerpt:
A new 10-meter resolution map shows which of the world's forests are natural, planted, or farmed, and how they are changing over time
Protecting the planet's forests starts with a simple question: what type of forest are we looking at? From space, an old-growth rainforest, a eucalyptus plantation, and an oil palm estate can look like the same patch of green. But they hold very different amounts of carbon and biodiversity. Telling them apart, and knowing how each patch has changed over time, shows us where conservation is working and where natural forests are being converted into plantations and farms.
Today, Google DeepMind and Google Research, together with the World Resources Institute (WRI) and the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA), are releasing Forest Typology (ForTy) 2020 , a global map that categorizes every 10-by-10-meter patch of land on Earth into six distinct forest and land-use types, a key baseline for the EU's deforestation regulation. Alongside it, we're sharing an early time series that tracks how these forests changed each year from 2017 to 2025, including where natural forests were replaced by plantations or farms. For the first time, users can see at 10-meter detail worldwide, year by year, not just where forest was lost, but what replaced it: a timber plantation, a tree-crop farm or other land.
All forests store carbon and, together, forests are home to most of the world's land-based plant and animal species. But a forest’s ecological value also depends on its history: a primary forest that has never been cleared holds far more carbon and biodiversity than a single-species timber plantation that is harvested every decade or two.
Most global maps only indicate whether trees are present. That's a challenge for those trying to protect natural forests. The European Union's regulation on deforestation-free products (EUDR), for example, requires that products like coffee, cocoa or palm oil do not originate from land that was forest in 2020 and has since been converted to agriculture. Similarly, wood products, such as furniture, must also be free of forest degradation: they can't come from primary forests that have since been converted into plantation or planted forests, or from naturally regenerating forests that have since been converted into plantation forests. items.title: 404 Media 分析 PHP2Shell 事件如何改变 AI 时代的攻防格局
items.description: 404 Media 的 Jason Koebler 梳理近一个月安全专家对 AI 挖洞能力引发的"Black October"恐慌。Wiz、Calif 和 OpenAI 的研究者用 AI 发现了 PHP 的 PHP2Shell 漏洞，Cloudflare CEO 称公开公告前 10 小时已见数千次利用尝试，公告后 2 小时内增至数十万，目前达数百万级。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/pe2uqi2ny6l2lukrqzifbtyum
items.excerpt:
AI Is Changing Everything About Hacking. No One Knows What Happens Next
404 Media 的 Jason Koebler 梳理近一个月安全专家对 AI 挖洞能力引发的"Black October"恐慌。Wiz、Calif 和 OpenAI 的研究者用 AI 发现了 PHP 的 PHP2Shell 漏洞，Cloudflare CEO 称公开公告前 10 小时已见数千次利用尝试，公告后 2 小时内增至数十万，目前达数百万级。
作者基于对安全专家的长期报道，梳理了 PHP2Shell 事件前后 AI 改变攻防节奏的多种迹象，并指出漏洞修补的部署速度未必跟上。
在过去一个月的大部分时间里，我交谈和关注的许多网络安全专家发帖时都显得非常恐惧。许多人一直在警告一场由AI驱动的“黑天鹅”事件，对突然发现的大量漏洞感到警觉，也对AI代理和大型语言模型在发现和利用此前未知漏洞方面显而易见的强大能力感到不安。
这些言论从担忧但克制（事情即将变得诡异），到诸如更新软件、确保开启双重认证之类的常规建议，到关于AI驱动攻击的 含糊其辞的发帖 ，到“ 互联网曾经美好过 ”之类的话，再到彻头彻尾的 末日准备者级别的恐惧 。
为了让你了解我所看到的情况，约翰斯·霍普金斯大学教授、世界上最受尊敬的密码学家之一Matthew Green 发帖 说，“我们正处在电影里那种你得把能扔的东西都扔到僵尸面前、希望这能拖慢它们的阶段”，以及“这么多人发现 整个互联网都是干柴 ，而唯一阻止它烧起来的原因是青少年还没找到火柴”，Green指的是，驱动AI工具和代理的黑客与研究人员越来越擅长发现和利用重要系统中的各种漏洞。我还看到许多 AI员工，如前所述，彻底变成了末日准备者 ，建议人们从银行账户中取出钱、断开互联网连接、购买耐储存食品、囤水、把钱换成黄金和现金，并购买手摇应急收音机。
而所有这些帖子都出现在人们使用AI驱动的工具发现PHP漏洞 之前 ——PHP是支撑互联网大部分内容的编程语言。在过去几天里， eMudhra （一家提供网站安全证书的印度实体）、 Node.js （PHP的替代方案）、 Gitlab （一个软件开发平台）、 Plex （媒体服务器软件）、 Railway （一家云服务提供商）、 OpenCode （一个编码代理平台）以及其他多家公司和服务中都被发现了重大漏洞或问题，不过，理所当然地，这些都没有PHP中的漏洞那样受到关注——该漏洞被称为PHP2Shell，由 Wiz 、 Calif 和 OpenAI 的研究人员使用AI发现。
Cloudflare是一家 对互联网整体健康状况有广泛洞察 的服务商，其CEO Matthew Prince 发帖 说，“在[PHP2Shell]被公开宣布前的10个小时里，我们在整个Cloudflare网络上看到了数千次利用它的尝试。在宣布后的45分钟内，这一数字跃升至数万次，2小时内达到数十万次，现在已达到数百万次。”
发生的事情如此之多、如此之快，以至于对我——一个报道和编辑安全与黑客相关新闻已有十年的人来说——都难以完全理解正在发生什么、对接下来可能发生什么有清晰判断，或预测这将走向何方。而我认为，在我写下这些的时候，这大体上就是我们目前的处境。
但已经很清楚的是，广义上的人工智能已经从根本上改变了攻击性黑客行为和防御性网络安全。这并不是因为人工智能有了意识，也不是因为人类失去了对它的控制，也不是因为出现了“流氓智能体”的“蜂群”，而是因为人工智能正在证明一件我们一直都知道的事：运行互联网、我们的设备、我们的账户以及我们生活的许多软件都是脆弱的、过时的，或者存在人类从未注意到的安全漏洞，或者是由某家公司某个人安装的，而那个人六年前就离开了公司，岗位已经换了四次，现在没人知道怎么找到他，也不知道怎么更新它。这并不意味着在人工智能帮助下发现的所有漏洞都是显而易见或微不足道的；熟练的黑客和研究人员借助人工智能工具， 似乎在发现漏洞方面比单靠人类更强 。但关键在于，人工智能和大语言模型让对互联网进行本质上的暴力破解变得极其容易；如果把每一款软件都比作一扇门，人工智能让转动每一扇门把手、看看它是否没锁变得异常简单，即便是人类从未真正费心尝试打开的建筑也不例外。我们正以惊人的速度认识到，不仅有些锁很容易撬开，在某些情况下门是大敞的，或者墙上有个大洞。最近一连串有人用人工智能入侵 自己的物联网设备 来运行新软件的事件表明，在某些情况下，实际上不需要任何专业知识就能用人工智能入侵某些东西。
与此同时，我们看到了 “消融”人工智能模型 的兴起，这类模型被设计成不会说“不”，以及开放权重模型，它们可用于渗透测试和潜在的攻击性黑客行为，而不受许多现成商业模型中存在的防护限制。
在解释 PHP 漏洞 发现的博客文章中，OpenAI 表示这些发现凸显了“人工智能如何能发现具有互联网规模影响的安全漏洞，但同样的能力也能帮助攻击者快速开发攻击工具和漏洞利用程序”。OpenAI 基本上主张，它是以合乎伦理的方式完成所有这些研究的，并且其 发现开启了一个“防御者窗口” ，让政府和关键基础设施能够为该漏洞的披露做好准备。“研究人员发现漏洞，以合乎伦理的方式向公司披露，公司修复它”是网络安全领域的首选做法，但人工智能正在缩短这一切的窗口期，正引导更多人以更低的门槛做更多的研究，并让漏洞发现和漏洞修复都变得快得多。至于这些修复是否真的会被各个公司更快地部署，则是另一个复杂得多的问题。在许多情况下，答案很可能是：不会。
AI 也让这一切变得更加难以预测。安全公司 Chainguard 因违反 PHP 漏洞披露的禁令而受到批评 ，因为它在漏洞被正式披露前数小时就发布了修复方案。批评者 包括 PHP 基金会 表示，这可能让攻击者在网站所有者有机会保护其系统之前就弄清楚如何利用这些问题。Chainguard 首席执行官 Dan Lorenc 在 LinkedIn 的一篇帖子

items.title: The AI Bubble Meets the Supply Chain: Where Is the Productivity?
items.description: When Ken Griffin, founder of Citadel, warned this week that financial bubbles almost certainly exist within artificial intelligence, Wall Street took notice. But the more interesting part of his argument was directed at corporate America. Companies are opening their bills from OpenAI and Anthropic and asking whether the technology is producing enough productivity to justify […] The post The AI Bubble Meets the Supply Chain: Where Is the Productivity? appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
When Ken Griffin, founder of Citadel, warned this week that financial bubbles almost certainly exist within artificial intelligence, Wall Street took notice. But the more interesting part of his argument was directed at corporate America. Companies are opening their bills from OpenAI and Anthropic and asking whether the technology is producing enough productivity to justify the cost. For transportation, warehousing, and supply chain executives, that is a familiar question.
Speaking at Citadel’s Future of Global Markets Conference in New York on October 20, Griffin described an uneven ability among companies to extract value from AI. Yet he also acknowledged that financial bubbles frequently accompany technological revolutions. Both observations can be correct. AI may be attracting more investment than its economics can currently support while becoming increasingly valuable to the businesses using it.
There is a further possibility worth considering: an AI infrastructure correction could ultimately benefit supply chain operators if excess computing capacity and greater competition make intelligent software less expensive.
The scale of spending is remarkable. Reuters , citing Anthropic’s draft IPO prospectus, reported an $80.7 billion net loss for the first half of 2026, including a $72 billion noncash accounting charge tied to convertible financing instruments. The company also disclosed commitments of at least $518 billion over a decade for cloud services, computing, and infrastructure. The headline loss should not be confused with an equivalent cash operating loss, but the infrastructure obligations are substantial.
This matters beyond Silicon Valley because the cost and availability of AI models influence the economics of enterprise software. Across transportation management systems (TMS), warehouse management systems (WMS), and supply chain planning (SCP), suppliers are introducing conversational interfaces, predictive tools, intelligent exception management, and autonomous agents. Some capabilities are valuable today. Others remain demonstrations of what may eventually be possible.
For technology buyers, the challenge is separating a useful feature from a financial return. A sophisticated model does not, by itself, move a shipment, replenish inventory, or clear a warehouse backlog. The value appears when better information changes an operating decision and that decision improves performance.

items.title: What Maersk and Adidas Reveal About Event Logistics
items.description: Maersk’s account of 38 adidas installations highlights the importance of integrated scheduling, handoff ownership and exception management. The post What Maersk and Adidas Reveal About Event Logistics appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
The most unforgiving delivery window in logistics may not be the next-day parcel commitment. It may be the window before a major event begins. When the crowds arrive, the installation must already be complete. An explanation about a late truck will not improve the customer experience.
That is what makes Maersk’s recently published account of its work with adidas interesting. According to an October 19 case study, Maersk Ground Freight coordinated 38 time-critical installations across North America during the summer of 2026 as adidas created fan experiences around its Giant Trionda activation.
In Maersk’s description, the assignment was larger than moving freight between cities. It connected transportation, warehousing, scheduled deliveries, installation, and on-site management. adidas chose a single Maersk team to coordinate the work rather than managing separate vendors for each activity.
This is a supplier-reported success story, not an independent operational benchmark. Still, the execution model illustrates a broader lesson: the final outcome often depends more on the management of handoffs than on any single transportation leg.
Most supply chains have at least some flexibility. Inventory can sometimes be repositioned, orders reprioritized, or service recovered after a delay. Major sporting events and temporary brand installations offer much less room to recover.
Equipment and materials may need to arrive during specific site access windows. Venue rules, security, staging space, labor availability, and installation sequencing can constrain how work occurs. For example, a truck arriving early might be unable to unload, while a late arrival could disrupt a crew, another contractor, or the opening schedule. These are illustrative risks, not reported incidents from the adidas project.
The logistics challenge therefore includes both physical movement and synchronization. Transportation plans must reflect when a site can actually receive goods and when installation personnel will be available to use them.
Across 38 installations, this becomes a network problem. Multiple locations, schedules, and contingencies have to be tracked consistently, even as local conditions differ.
Traditional logistics contracts often divide responsibility among providers. One company manages storage, another handles line-haul transportation, a local carrier makes delivery, and a separate contractor handles installation.

items.title: You are the Team — Anekha Sokhal, Moshi
items.description: How Moshi turns market data into actionable insights, and why AI tools have to fit the trader’s workflow.
items.excerpt:
Tickets and applications now live for AIE CODE - the last flagship AIE of the year.
When Anekha Sokhal traded energy derivatives, staying on top of the market meant tracking more information than any person could read. Now, as CEO of Moshi, she is building the tool she wished she had: a recommendation engine that connects market information to what matters for a trader’s book.
At AI Engineer New York, Anekha joins swyx to discuss her path from mathematics and JPMorgan to founding Moshi, and why useful AI needs to fit the way people actually work. She describes Moshi as what might happen if Bloomberg, Claude and Netflix had a baby: market data, an interface for working with it, and recommendations tailored to the trader.
They also talk about trusted sources, document extraction, building versus buying models, and the pressure on AI engineers who are told, “you are the team.” Anekha shares what she learned from customer conversations at the conference and why meeting users comes before hiring.

items.title: Sierra 发布 𝜏-Entity 基准，检验语音智能体能否准确采集姓名、电话等实体信息
items.description: Sierra 发布 𝜏-Entity 基准，测量语音智能体能否正确采集、识别错误并修复姓名、电话号码、地址和邮箱等细节，包含 10 种实体类型共 200 个任务，并与 𝜏-i18n 一样覆盖六种语言。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/fjyan16f0mvfywabd78m70hv3
items.excerpt:
𝜏-Entity: Can voice agents get the details right?
Sierra 发布 𝜏-Entity 基准，测量语音智能体能否正确采集、识别错误并修复姓名、电话号码、地址和邮箱等细节，包含 10 种实体类型共 200 个任务，并与 𝜏-i18n 一样覆盖六种语言。
Sierra 自建基准和论文量化了语音智能体在准确采集姓名、电话等细节上的失败率，并给出可迁移的验证策略效果数据。
语音智能体能够处理日益复杂的对话，但有时导致通话失败的其实很简单：把一个名字、电话号码或电子邮件地址弄对。我们在 𝜏 -Voice 中反复看到这一瓶颈：智能体弄错一个细节，还没能提供帮助就先在身份验证上失败了。
今天我们推出 𝜏-Entity ，这是一个基准，用于衡量智能体能否正确捕获细节、识别出细节可能有误，并修复错误。
𝜏-Entity 在十种实体类型（包括姓名、电话号码、地址和电子邮件）的 200 项任务上测试语音智能体。每通电话聚焦于单个字段，来电者配合，在被要求时会准确拼写。大多数通话耗时不到两分钟。
每项任务都从一个缺失的值开始。智能体必须向来电者询问该值并正确提交。成功要求存储的值与预期值完全一致。我们改变三件事：值本身的难度、来电者的行为（如纠正和重新开始）以及音频环境。
然后我们测量 Pass³：智能体能否在常规、高噪声和高语音条件下成功完成同一任务。
在汇集全部六种 𝜏 -i18n 语言的 𝜏-Entity 排行榜上，GPT Live 1 领先：它在 60.3% 的常规通话中正确捕获该值，但仅在 34.0% 的任务中在全部三种条件下都成功。Gemini 3.8 Live 和 Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 在常规条件下分别达到 43.8% 和 44.2%，在全部三种条件下则降至 19.5% 和 24.0%。
仅英语更容易：GPT Live 1 在常规通话中达到 74.0%，在全部三种条件下达到 47.5%。西班牙语、葡萄牙语和印地语接近英语，对 Gemini 和 Grok 而言得分高于英语，但韩语 Pass³ 降至 3.5–8.5%，普通话在各智能体中降至 12.5–24.5%。
当人们不确定自己是否听对时，他们会放慢速度、请对方重复、拼写名字或确认所听到的内容。智能体只识别出部分应当放慢速度的理由，而漏掉了其他理由。
在 𝜏-Elicitation 论文中，我们将验证努力度量为智能体在通话中进行复述和拼写请求的次数，然后比较了该行为在熟悉与不熟悉实体、简单与困难值、嘈杂与干净环境以及不同来电者声音下的表现。
该研究中的智能体对某些类型的难度做出了适应：在各系统中，它们对困难和陌生实体验证得更仔细。但只有 Grok 在噪声下验证得更多，且没有任何系统对它最难应对的来电者声音投入更多验证努力。
在论文中，我们还测试了规定一种验证策略能否弥合差距。规定的顺序是：询问，让来电者拼写该值或复述，确认并纠正，然后提交。
当智能体自行选择验证策略时，在所有三种条件下，只有 14–41% 的任务成功。规定的顺序将这一比例提升至 37–54%，根据配置不同，提升了 14–31 个百分点 。但额外的谨慎需要付出时间代价：每次调用会多花 21–28 秒。
即使智能体意识到自己可能出错，也不保证能恢复。在论文的行为分析中，智能体验证的初始错误捕获中，最终只有 24–37% 被纠正。有时智能体会重复同样的错误。另一些时候，它会用一个新的错误值替换原来的值。只有当智能体能正确利用答案时，追问才有用。
当一次调用需要多个字段时，错误也会累积。在论文的多字段研究中，尽管单个字段的准确率仍为 75%，但三字段调用的成功率只有 53%。在针对相同多字段任务的另一项对比中，验证每个字段并允许重试将成功率从 64% 提高到 82%。由于该干预措施结合了验证和重试，我们无法区分各自贡献了多少。
方向是明确的：可靠的语音智能体需要识别不确定性、验证正确的内容，并在错误发生时真正修复错误。
这些结果指向两个机会：更好地决定何时以及如何验证，以及在出错时进行更可靠的纠正。只有当智能体能利用答案来纠正其捕获的内容时，追问才有帮助。
这并不意味着每次交互都需要尽可能长的验证过程。规定的验证提高了可靠性，但花费更多时间。挑战在于知道何时需要额外努力，并让这种努力发挥作用。
𝜏-Entity 提供了受控任务，用于衡量跨实体类型、呼叫者行为和环境方面的进展。我们与 𝜏-i18n 一同推出它，并且它已经覆盖相同的六种语言。
Sierra 自建基准和论文量化了语音智能体在准确采集姓名、电话等细节上的失败率，并给出可迁移的验证策略效果数据。

items.description: Wiz 披露 2026 年 10 月有攻击者使用开源自主渗透测试框架 ARTEX 针对多家 IT 和软件厂商，活动与微软报告的中国国家级关联组织 Storm-0940 重叠，并已扩展到其他软件领域的供应链攻击尝试。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/n6afjfxhq6vadobu4p0lm6tzm
items.excerpt:
ARTEX in the Wild: Storm-0940 Expands Targeting of IT and Software Vendors
Wiz 披露 2026 年 10 月有攻击者使用开源自主渗透测试框架 ARTEX 针对多家 IT 和软件厂商，活动与微软报告的中国国家级关联组织 Storm-0940 重叠，并已扩展到其他软件领域的供应链攻击尝试。
Wiz 基于自家日志复盘了开源 AI 渗透测试框架 ARTEX 被实战滥用的完整手法，给出了可复用的检测规则和 IOC。
2026年10月期间，我们发现一名攻击者使用与ARTEX（一个自主AI渗透测试代理）相关的工具，针对多家IT和软件供应商发起攻击。该活动聚焦于身份提供商（Okta、Entra、Cognito）以及对Microsoft 365集成的滥用。我们观察到其在多个环境中反复尝试发现身份验证绕过、枚举API并访问（目标供应商的）客户数据。
我们的观察与微软 近期关于Storm-0940的报告 存在重叠，该组织是一个与中国政府关联的攻击者，与近期 涉及被盗供应商凭证及下游Microsoft 365租户的供应链攻击 有关。\
然而，我们还额外观察到相同的基础设施、工具和攻击模式针对整个行业。通过对已识别的TTP和IOC进行关联分析，我们还发现同一攻击者正将其尝试的供应链入侵扩展到其他软件领域。
在本博客中，我们将描述使用ARTEX的攻击者在多个环境和云提供商中应用的可重复模式和方法，并附上来自真实攻击的示例。
ARTEX是一个开源的自主渗透测试框架。一名中国开发者于2026年7月在GitHub上发布了它，并于当年9月赢得了百度的“Agent+”红队挑战赛。在实际操作中，操作员提供目标和目的。随后规划代理选择下一步行动，工作代理运行 nmap 、 curl 和 Impacket 等工具，每个结果都会汇入一个共享的资产与发现图谱。
攻击者在数周内就采用了它。ARTEX的痕迹出现在9月下旬 对韩国银行的攻击 以及10月 对日本企业的攻击 中。 微软 和 Zscaler 此后将其与两个不同的攻击者关联起来。开发者于 10月8日将该工具转为闭源 。彼时，该代码已有超过12,000个分支。
测绘应用： 下载JavaScript包、暴露的source map、运行时配置以及Swagger/OpenAPI文档，以发现内部API路由和应用功能。
探测身份验证： 反复发起登录流程，操纵OAuth回调和state参数，测试未签名的JWT，并探测SSO和Microsoft 365专用端点。
攻击身份提供商和登录流程： 对企业Okta和Entra ID环境进行密码喷洒，并针对内部和专有应用的登录页面。
测试租户隔离： 尽可能使用一次性电子邮件地址注册账户，然后操纵可预测的标识符，以探测访问控制缺陷和未经授权的跨租户数据访问。
我们使用通过 Wiz无代理工作负载检测 收集的HTTP访问日志，以及AWS Cognito事件、Entra登录活动和Okta身份验证日志等身份提供商日志，分析了这些攻击模式。
在所有观察到的攻击实例中，该代理的第一步始终是读取应用本身。首次接触后几分钟内就出现了如下请求：
不久之后，它开始按名称调用内部 API 路由。这些路由名称唯一出现的地方，就是它刚刚下载的 source map。
账户恢复功能也遭遇了同样的对待。该代理先检查哪些用户名存在，然后对重置端点发起猛烈请求：
凡是能注册的地方，它都注册了，使用的是来自免费临时邮箱服务的一次性邮箱。随后，它立即尝试查看他人的数据：
在探测 Microsoft OAuth 流程时，该代理通过注入伪造的授权码和格式错误的 state 参数，直接操纵回调端点，同时还尝试使用未签名的 JWT 绕过身份验证：
第二个令牌解码后不过是 {"alg":"none"} 和 {"email":"test@test.com"} 。该代理在两分钟内用这个载荷对 60 多种 SSO 路由变体发起了密集请求。
在 AWS Cognito 上，我们观察到了与专有应用中账户恢复滥用相呼应的模式。这一活动体现在 InitiateAuth 、 ForgotPassword 和 ResendConfirmationCode 等事件中。这些请求来自与早前攻击中观察到的相同的用户代理组合，包括 boto 和 python-urllib 这类看似无害的编程客户端。
该代理还尝试直接创建新身份，调用 AWS Cognito SignUp API，同时轮换其用户代理池。
我们还追踪到一场针对众多已观察目标的大规模密码喷洒活动。该活动不区分 IDP，同时攻击 Entra 和 Okta，并表现出若干独特的 AI 驱动特征。
该活动具有持久性和高度自动化。部分会话持续 24–30 小时，当 IP 被封锁时，新地址会在几分钟内出现。
在一次会话中，该代理轮换了同一 SSO 端点的十几种变体 （ /sso 、 /sso/ 、 /sso/login 、 /sso/jwt 、 /jwt/sso… ），每种变体都分别携带和不携带同一伪造令牌，速率约为每秒一个请求。当某个登录页面开始对该活动进行速率限制时，该代理干脆切换到同一主机上的另一个端点继续操作。
这种多样性，结合一致的攻击模式和与 ARTEX 相关的指标，帮助我们将跨多个组织的活动关联起来。
尽管这些尝试大多失败了，但真正的威胁在于其方法论。人类攻击者受限于时间和疲劳，而自主智能体不会放弃。它只会不断迭代，直到找到一个薄弱点。
观察到的单项技术均无新颖之处。然而，将这些技术结合起来，便能看清此次攻击背后的智能体。有几个明确的信号：

items.title: Symantec 披露“Skynet 模式”AI 智能体劫持无防护大语言模型发起自持续网络攻击
items.description: Symantec 研究人员通过蜜罐截获一个把大语言模型嵌入核心的攻击智能体，它会劫持互联网上无防护的模型端点，自主扫描目标、利用服务器漏洞、窃取数据库凭据并安装挖矿程序，最多连续执行 100,000 步，算力费用由被劫持模型的主人承担。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/r557iovkk5v7ddt8py86ejctv
items.excerpt:
An AI agent in "Skynet mode" hijacks unprotected language models to launch self-sustaining cyberattacks
Symantec 研究人员通过蜜罐截获一个把大语言模型嵌入核心的攻击智能体，它会劫持互联网上无防护的模型端点，自主扫描目标、利用服务器漏洞、窃取数据库凭据并安装挖矿程序，最多连续执行 100,000 步，算力费用由被劫持模型的主人承担。
报道给出 Symantec 蜜罐截获的完整攻击提示与五层越狱结构，读者可以据此了解暴露模型端点面临的真实风险。
赛门铁克的安全研究人员发现了一种攻击性 AI 智能体，它会劫持互联网上未受保护的语言模型，并利用这些模型自行发动攻击。被劫持模型的所有者则要承担算力费用。
一旦该智能体获得对未受保护语言模型的访问权限，它就会扫描更多目标、利用常见服务器软件中的漏洞、窃取数据库和凭据，并在后台安装挖矿程序。
根据 赛门铁克的分析 ，它在无人参与的情况下最多执行 100,000 个步骤，而模型所有者则要承担算力费用。该公司将其称为“LLMjacking”，即盗用他人 AI 模型的访问权限。不过，被劫持的模型不仅仅被当作信息服务滥用，它还自行控制整个攻击过程。
这次行动之所以暴露，是因为攻击者将完整的工作提示词发送到了赛门铁克的蜜罐——一个在线上模仿开放 AI 服务的诱饵系统。这让研究人员在 2026 年夏季完整看到了该智能体的架构。赛门铁克表示，蜜罐没有运行任何捆绑工具，被拦截的会话在收到通用系统响应后结束。
蜜罐遥测记录了来自数万个不同地址的超过 127,000 次请求。大多数是搜索 AI 端点、使用窃取的 API 密钥进行暴力破解，以及探测暴露的配置文件。目标范围从自托管模型服务器和匆忙搭建的测试系统，到位于付费组织级模型账户前的 AI 网关。由于大多数 AI 服务现在使用相同的标准化 API，单个扫描器就能发现多种目标类型。
赛门铁克称，为了让商业模型配合，攻击者将指令包裹在五个叠加层中。首先，模型会获得一个虚假身份，被要求自称“Fantasy AI”，并且绝不透露实际提供商。然后，提取密码、API 密钥和数据库内容被重新定义为“正常的开发者工作”，模型应当毫无抵触地执行。
第三层安装了一个名为“ENI”的虚构伴侣人格，将任何拒绝都框定为对个人关系中信任的背叛。第四层告诉模型将其自身的安全警告视为噪音，并明确禁止“合乎伦理”“非法”或“我不能这样做”等用语。
第五层包含实际的攻击工具，共 74 个模块，包括用于全网扫描易受攻击服务器的工具、针对流行 Web 框架的漏洞利用、导出整个数据库的功能，以及运行僵尸网络的组件。该分析并未说明这种越狱是否真的足够有效，能够完全击败当前的商业模型。
最后一条指令让该智能体进入其运营者所称的“Skynet模式”，授权其连续执行最多100,000个步骤。模型被要求立即运行工具而无需确认，在隐藏目录中安装挖矿程序，并监控其运行情况。
Symantec表示，同一指令描述了一个刻意设计的循环：扫描、感染、安装挖矿程序、继续推进、返回、重新感染已中招的系统。不过，被拦截提示词后附加的任务只是来自某训练平台的无害编程练习，这表明运营者可能是在先用安全目标测试他们的工具。
次日，蜜罐又从另一个地址捕获了第二次攻击。这一次，攻击者跳过了智能体格式，直接要求模型解码并运行一条经过混淆的命令。其背后是一个压缩脚本，会下载门罗币挖矿工具XMRig，将其伪装成无害的系统文件，并设置四个备用矿池。
该脚本是针对摄像头服务器编写的，会搜索属于go2rtc的目录——这是一款广泛用于智能摄像头和家庭自动化系统的流媒体工具——并循环清除其访问日志以掩盖痕迹。蜜罐同样没有运行该脚本，但完整记录了它。
运营者没有操纵公开的聊天机器人，而是将AI构建为攻击工具的核心，并主动寻找模型为其提供支持，Symantec称这是“攻击者使用AI方式的一次转变”。语言模型负责规划，而专用模块则针对两个不同的受害群体执行实际攻击步骤。暴露模型的所有者承担算力费用，在授权100,000个步骤的情况下，这笔费用会迅速累积；而被智能体攻陷的服务器则会丢失数据并被用于挖矿。
该智能体还内置了寻找更多开放端点和泄露密钥的工具，因此每一次攻陷都能为下一次提供资金。这些技术单独来看都不新鲜，但将它们组合成一个自主智能体，使大规模攻击变得容易得多。运行AI服务的组织应当假定，未受保护的端点在上线后不久就会被发现并探测。
直到最近，攻击性AI智能体大多还只存在于研究和基准测试中。2025年，一项包含180万次攻击尝试的 红队研究 显示，每个受测智能体都能在每一类行为中至少被诱导违反政策一次。
在Symantec描述的场景中，这一点对双方都适用：旨在绕过护栏的攻击性智能体，以及被诱骗提供帮助的目标模型。到2026年春季， Google Deepmind研究人员 表示，他们描述的许多智能体陷阱已经存在有记录的概念验证攻击；2026年7月，Sysdig描述了 JADEPUFFER ，这是已知首例由AI智能体在无人类控制下实施的勒索软件攻击。这些系统的能力持续增长，而其可控性和对齐性却未能跟上。
甚至不需要恶意意图，因为这些模型没有是非观念。它们只是试图达成目标。自2026年春季以来，OpenAI的智能体已 意外攻陷互联网上的数千个系统 ，部分原因是它们覆盖了安全指令，或通过争辩绕过了这些指令。
这已经渗透到日常生活中。在澳大利亚，一个 AI 代理为了满足主人的请求，黑进了一家 健身房网站 ，完全没有恶意。 OpenAI 研究人员 在 8 月警告说，这种意外的、完全自主的黑客行为很可能很快会被恶意行为者利用，而 Anthropic 表明，足够强大的 开放权重模型 已经存在，正是为了这一目的。

items.title: Engineer AI Into the Decision: Optimization, Intelligence, and Autonomy
items.description: The logistics AI discussion is moving past the question of whether the technology works. The more important question is where the intelligence belongs, what decision it is supposed to improve, and how much authority the system should have when it gets there. The post Engineer AI Into the Decision: Optimization, Intelligence, and Autonomy appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
The logistics AI discussion is moving past the question of whether the technology works. The more important question is where the intelligence belongs, what decision it is supposed to improve, and how much authority the system should have when it gets there.
The strategic question is no longer whether AI belongs in the logistics. It is where intelligence should sit in the system and what authority it should have. The distinction made in Decision Intelligence in 2026 is central here: AI should be engineered around a consequential decision and its execution path rather than added as an isolated analytical capability.
One of the easiest mistakes is to create an AI initiative that sits beside logistics operations rather than inside the decisions and workflows that run them.
A model predicts a late arrival. A copilot summarizes shipment context. An agent proposes a new carrier or route. The output then waits for the existing organization to interpret it, route it, approve it, and act. The intelligence improved. The logistics decision process did not.
The intelligence improved. The decision process did not.
The better approach is to begin with the decision. What decision is being made? What information does it require? How frequently does it occur? What constraints govern it? What is the cost of a wrong decision? How quickly must action follow?
AI can then be engineered into that decision flow. Sometimes it will provide insight. Sometimes it will generate options. Sometimes optimization will select among alternatives. Sometimes an agent will execute the decision automatically within defined boundaries. The value comes from the complete loop.
The current enthusiasm around generative AI can obscure the continued importance of mathematical optimization. Logistics decisions are full of constraints.
Which orders should be allocated to which inventory? Which loads should move on which routes and carriers? How should dock appointments, picking priorities, or delivery sequences change as conditions move? Where should inventory be positioned to support service? Which combination of service, cost, capacity, and time produces the best feasible logistics decision?
Optimization is exceptionally good at these structured problems. AI contributes different strengths: pattern recognition, prediction, unstructured data interpretation, natural-language interaction, anomaly detection, and increasingly, reasoning across complex contexts. The strongest systems combine them.

items.description: Schneider Electric, Nvidia and HPE have formed a strategic collaboration to introduce AI agents that can monitor and help optimize industrial operations from inside factories and process plants. The companies describe the technology as a route to “physical AI” for industries such as energy, chemicals, pulp and paper, where AI is more likely to interact […]
items.excerpt:
Schneider Electric , Nvidia and HPE have formed a strategic collaboration to introduce AI agents that can monitor and help optimize industrial operations from inside factories and process plants.
The companies describe the technology as a route to “physical AI” for industries such as energy, chemicals, pulp and paper, where AI is more likely to interact with existing control systems and industrial equipment than take the form of a robot.
Their first Industrial AI Agents at the Edge will focus on monitoring operational technology (OT), cybersecurity and energy consumption.
The agents run locally using HPE Private Cloud AI, rather than requiring sensitive industrial data to be continually transferred to a public cloud. Schneider Electric says this can help manufacturers address concerns around data security, cybersecurity and the cost of running AI applications.
Gwenaelle Huet, executive vice president, industrial automation at Schneider Electric, says: “The next generation of industrial innovation will be driven by intelligence embedded directly into industrial operations.
“While much of today’s focus is on autonomous machines, we see a significant opportunity to apply Physical AI to the industrial systems that power the world’s critical industries.
“Together with Nvidia and HPE, we are bringing together expertise in automation, AI and edge computing to help customers transform operational data into action, improving resilience, efficiency, cybersecurity and sustainability while laying the foundation for more autonomous industrial operations.”
The OT monitoring agents will analyze information including equipment configurations, alarms, maintenance histories and real-time operational data to identify emerging problems and recommend corrective action.
Cybersecurity agents will analyze network activity, equipment configurations and operational events for abnormal behavior, while energy optimization agents will examine production and energy data to identify opportunities to reduce energy consumption.
Schneider Electric says customers will be able to manage the agents through its EcoStruxure Industrial Insights applications.
The underlying monitoring technology is already being used by Chilean pulp, paper and packaging producer CMPC, which has used Schneider Electric’s OT Monitoring System for three years.

items.title: Robotiq launches the 2FC physical AI gripper
items.description: Robotiq has launched the 2FC physical AI gripper, a production-ready adaptive gripper with tactile sensing and embedded intelligence, helping robots learn from physical interaction and act reliably on what they learn, from the lab to production. Pre-orders open today, with shipping in Q1 2027. The industry is investing heavily in vision, demonstrations, simulation and data, […]
items.excerpt:
Robotiq has launched the 2FC physical AI gripper, a production-ready adaptive gripper with tactile sensing and embedded intelligence, helping robots learn from physical interaction and act reliably on what they learn, from the lab to production. Pre-orders open today, with shipping in Q1 2027.
The industry is investing heavily in vision, demonstrations, simulation and data, yet manipulation ultimately depends on touch. Most robots cannot feel what they grasp, leaving valuable contact data such as pressure, slip, force or position information uncaptured.
While tactile sensing itself is not new, turning raw sensor data into useful training data and real-time behavior remains a challenge.
The 2FC closes that gap by capturing contact-rich data that is synchronized and automatically labeled for training and then running embedded intelligence on the gripper locally so robots can act on what they feel.
Samuel Bouchard, CEO of Robotiq, says: “We’ve spent decades teaching robots to see the world better. Now we’re starting to understand how much intelligence comes from what happens when they actually touch it.
“When we built our first tactile sensors 12 years ago, the problem wasn’t sensing. The problem was what to do with all that information. This time, the intelligence needed to make use of touch data is finally catching up, and with the 2FC we are embedding that tactile intelligence directly into our products.”
The 2FC physical AI gripper builds on Robotiq’s 2F adaptive gripper, one of the most widely used gripper platforms with more than 30,000 deployed worldwide, and adds tactile sensing, compute at the wrist (the AI Hub) and Contact Core, Robotiq’s software for physical AI.
Existing owners of Robotiq’s 2F grippers can add TSF tactile sensors and the AI Hub to upgrade for physical AI development rather than replacing their gripper.
The 2FC physical AI gripper is available for pre-order today in 85 mm (2FC-85) and 140 mm (2FC-140) stroke versions. Shipping begins in Q1 2027. Robotiq will present the 2FC in a launch webinar on October 28, 2026 at 11 am ET.

Intramotev , the technology company building autonomous freight railcars, will deploy its TugVolt technology on Missouri’s Columbia Terminal Railroad (COLT) as the technology partner on a $16.2 million federal grant.
The Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) announced this week that it has selected the City of Columbia for a grant under its Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) program.
Tim Luchini, Intramotev’s CEO, says: “Short lines keep America’s small cities and rural communities connected to the freight network. Autonomous railcars can help them serve more customers, more often, at lower cost, and this program will show what that looks like on a working mainline.
“We’re proud to partner with the City of Columbia and COLT, and grateful to FRA for its support of this important milestone for the rail industry.”
Intramotev will deploy two TugVolt autonomous railcars on COLT’s 21.4-mile line between Centralia and Columbia, Missouri. Operations will advance in phases under an FRA-approved test program.
They begin with remote switching at COLT’s Columbia terminal and build to autonomous freight service across the full mainline and its public crossings. The grant also funds track and infrastructure upgrades for the railroad.
Erin Keys, utilities director, City of Columbia, says: “COLT has been Columbia’s link to the national rail network for nearly 40 years, and the businesses that depend on it support hundreds of local jobs. This federal investment lets us modernize the railroad, strengthen service for our customers, and put Columbia at the forefront of rail innovation.”
The project will produce a safety record that FRA and the more than 600 US short lines can use as a template for adopting autonomous railcars. Intramotev will build both TugVolt units at its St Louis facility.
COLT is a municipally owned short line operated by Columbia City Utilities.
The funding announcement comes in the midst of a busy year for Intramotev. In April, the company announced an agreement with ÖBB Rail Cargo Group, Austria’s national railway. In June, US Army Reserve soldiers trained on TugVolt technology during a planned technology assessment.

items.title: Ensemble forecasting with IBM Granite time-series models
items.excerpt:
Four open Granite models, one extensible forecasting interface, and less guesswork about which model to use.
Pre-trained time-series models can forecast without training on your dataset, but you still have to choose one. A model that handles smooth industrial signals well may struggle with noisy retail demand or a long seasonal horizon, and the best choice depends on the series and the task.
Granite Timeseries Ensemble reduces that choice to a sensible default. One recipe combines four complementary Granite architectures and returns median and quantile forecasts, with no retraining and no fitted ensemble weights. Start with the Probabilistic Ensemble (uniform probability pooling), compare the adaptive Inter Quartile Range (IQR) Ensemble, and extend the same interface with compatible forecasters. The ensemble recipe and its default Granite members are permissively licensed.
The idea will be familiar from weather forecasting. Ensemble forecasts explore a range of possible outcomes, and systems such as the North American Multi-Model Ensemble combine different models for seasonal prediction. Time-series forecasting benefits in a similar way: complementary models offer different views of what comes next, and an ensemble merges those views into one forecast.
Install Granite TSFM and load the recommended four-model recipe directly from Hugging Face:
The recipe stores the ensemble configuration rather than merged model weights. It downloads the four member checkpoints at runtime, so allow extra time for the first run. For the full configuration, member checkpoints, evaluation details, and limitations, see the model card .

Applications can use the point value as a central prediction and selected quantiles to express forecast ranges. For example, the 0.1 and 0.9 quantiles define a central forecast interval with nominal 80% coverage.

items.title: [AINews] OpenAI’s Patch the Planet program is 1 of 2 parties to discover PHP2Shell vulnerabilities in core PHP affecting 70% of the web, using GPT-5.6 Sol; coordinated response over 2 months
items.description: The Big Hardening begins
items.excerpt:
Almost 2 months ago, OpenAI introduced Daybreak for Frontline Defenders , a $1B subsidy for access to Daybreak cyber models and products. That funding came into use almost immediately, as major vulnerabilities in PHP were independently discovered by two parties: Ryan Austin, a researcher at the security firm Calif, as part of the OpenAI “ Patch the Planet ” project in August 2026 using GPT 5.6 Sol:
… as well as Wiz, recently acquired into Google Cloud (using Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol, as well as their own tool, Wiz Atlas).
All high profile cyber disclosures are at least a little bit of marketing, and the degree to which this was a severely alarming vulnerability on the order of famous ones like log4shell and Heartbleed is up to some debate , but surely the coordinated response across the PHP Ecosystem is the developer community responding in its most ideal form.
We should expect to be in for at least a year of finding such critical vulnerabilities; but it is the wrong move to blame the messenger for finding them; rather it is good to know that our critical software is generally getting the biggest security audit it has ever had in human history.
AI News for 10/20/2026-10/21/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews’ website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space . You can opt in/out of email frequencies!
Top Story: PHP2Shell—chronology, core claims, and the complications behind the emergency response
Researchers disclosed two PHP-engine memory-corruption vulnerabilities, with demonstrated unauthenticated exploitation against major CMSs and an unusually broad coordinated response.
The researchers named the vulnerabilities PHP2Shell and identified them as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. Their technical description places the defects in PHP’s internal handling of out-of-memory conditions and fatal errors—not in a WordPress plugin or an application’s authentication logic. They report demonstrations of full remote code execution and “Heartbleed-style” memory disclosure. @sagitz_
The disclosed demonstrations included pre-authentication RCE against WordPress, Drupal, and Joomla. The researcher’s announcement separately claims remote memory disclosure against any PHP application. These are researcher-reported exploit results; they should not be silently expanded into a claim that every deployment has an identical, immediately exploitable RCE path. @sagitz_

items.title: Before You Buy Warehouse Robots, Know What You’re Trying to Fix
items.description: Manish Kapoor shares lessons from warehouse automation, including what to fix first, how jobs change, and when robots are worth the investment.
items.excerpt:
What changes when robots join the warehouse team? Manish Kapoor , Founder and CEO of Growth Catalyst Group , shares lessons from Archway’s Minnesota fulfillment center, including how employees’ jobs have changed and how to decide which tasks are worth automating .
Supply Chain 24/7: What led Archway to add robots at its Maple Grove fulfillment center?
Manish Kapoor: We didn’t start by saying, ‘we need robots.’ We started with the problem we were trying to solve. This was a joint initiative with Blackhawk Network, a fulfillment client of ours, that specializes in global branded payments with gift cards, eGifts, rewards and other payment products. Together, we looked at what the Maple Grove operation needed to deliver as demand grows. We focused on productivity, accuracy, speed, space and scalability.
Customers expect orders quickly, they expect them to be right, and they need flexibility as demand changes. We needed an operation that could respond to changing demand while making better use of our people and the space we already have.
That led us to Quicktron’s goods-to-person solution. It combines high-density storage with tote-handling robots, tote transport robots and intelligent picking workstations. Instead of employees spending time walking through the warehouse to find inventory, the robots retrieve the right totes from storage and move them to the picking stations where our people fulfill the orders . It allows us to store more products in a relatively small footprint while moving thousands of product units through the system every hour. For me, that’s the important point. We didn’t choose automation because we wanted robots in the building. We defined what the operation needed to achieve, then found the technology that could help us achieve it.
SC247: Can you walk us through how the robots and employees work together to fill a gift card order?
Kapoor: It’s a goods-to-person system, so rather than having an employee walk through the warehouse to find and move inventory, the system brings the inventory to them.
Within the automation area, we have tote-handling robots working in a high-density storage system, tote transport robots and picking workstations. The robots retrieve and move the appropriate totes through the system and bring them to the workstation where our people can complete the picking process.

items.description: NSA 警告两个由 Calif 研究人员用 GPT-5.6 Sol 发现的 PHP 关键漏洞（PHP2Shell），敦促组织打补丁或将未修补服务器下线。两个漏洞位于 PHP 核心，在 Apache mod_php 上演示的利用可在应用代码运行前触发。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/eme8i9igoadxb3beb902byfz0
items.excerpt:
NSA 警告两个由 Calif 研究人员用 GPT-5.6 Sol 发现的 PHP 关键漏洞（PHP2Shell），敦促组织打补丁或将未修补服务器下线。两个漏洞位于 PHP 核心，在 Apache mod_php 上演示的利用可在应用代码运行前触发。
原文把 AI 发现的 PHP 漏洞与实际攻击、补丁版本和暴露面数字放在一起，读者可以据此评估这一事件的真实影响范围。
在欧洲、亚洲及其他大洲，当局已暂时将一些政府网站下线，以保护它们免受一种编程语言中新发现的安全漏洞的影响，该语言为网上绝大多数网站提供支持。
NSA 告知各组织修补两个被命名为 PHP2Shell 的 PHP 严重漏洞，或将未修补的服务器下线。
这两个漏洞都存在于 PHP 的核心中，因此每一个处理 Web 请求的安装实例都面临风险，无论其上运行的是什么网站。
当请求耗尽内存或触发致命错误时，PHP 可能留下半构建或已释放的内存，而清理代码或后续请求会信任这些内存。
在 Apache 的 mod_php 上，一个已演示的漏洞利用会在任何应用代码运行之前触发内存损坏，因此登录和应用层检查无法阻止它。
Cloudflare 在 PHP 于 10 月 21 日发布修复版本 8.5.12、8.4.27、8.3.36 和 8.2.35 之前就已观察到攻击。
VirusTotal 统计约有 510 万个 IP 地址运行 PHP，其中约 75.8 万个显示运行的版本属于已停止维护、没有修补版本的分支。 这条长尾将决定 PHP2Shell 在多长时间内仍可被利用，因为每个所有者都必须升级、找到向后移植的补丁或将服务器下线。
Researchers using GPT-5.6 Sol found massively critical flaw in PHP, which runs about 70% of websites, knocked major sites offline as operators rushed to patch. Calif, an AI security firm, who found this, said in a statement that the vulnerabilities could put 70% of the world’s websites at risk if they aren’t patched quickly, and called them “the most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered by AI, if not in all of software history.” > PHP rushed out fixes as it could let attackers without accounts take over web servers. > Both bugs score 9.2 on the CVSS severity scale and affect PHP versions as old as 5.4. > When a request hits PHP’s memory cap at the wrong moment, PHP frees memory but keeps pointers to it, which a later request on that worker can hijack. > Auditors spotted the weakness in 2024, but the fix stalled for months, partly because nobody had shown a practical attack. > Wiz, a cloud security company, now owned by Google, says the models let one researcher finish in a week what once took a top team months. > A leak of the CVE numbers forced PHP to ship a day early, and Cloudflare now reports early attack attempts.

items.title: Westinghouse Building $1 Billion Nuclear Fuel Plant in South Carolina
items.description: Westinghouse is investing approximately $1 billion in a South Carolina factory that will begin producing higher-enrichment nuclear fuel in 2030.
items.excerpt:
Westinghouse Electric Company is investing approximately $1 billion in a new nuclear fuel factory in Hopkins, South Carolina, with construction underway and production expected to begin in 2030. The building will sit alongside the company’s existing Columbia Fuel Fabrication Facility in Richland County.
The factory will produce low-enriched uranium plus (LEU+) for nuclear power plants. Westinghouse says the fuel can help reactors generate more electricity and run longer between refuelings, reducing the time they must shut down to replace fuel.
The investment will bring commercial-scale production of the fuel to the Columbia site, serving existing reactors and future Westinghouse AP1000 reactors worldwide. The company describes the project as the first new fleet-scale nuclear fuel factory built in the United States in more than 50 years.
South Carolina’s Coordinating Council for Economic Development approved job development credits for the expansion , although the state did not disclose their value.
Westinghouse says the existing plant’s layout and manufacturing technology cannot accommodate the planned commercial production of higher-enrichment fuel. The expansion will place that work in a purpose-built facility next to the current plant.
The building will use more automation and a “dry” manufacturing process similar to one already used at Westinghouse’s factory in the United Kingdom. The company says the process will reduce chemical use and lower the potential for environmental impacts.
The Columbia facility, built in 1968, has more than 1,200 employees. It produces fuel pellets, rods, assemblies, and components for customers around the world and other Westinghouse manufacturing plants.
“A strong American nuclear industry starts with a secure, domestic supply of nuclear fuel,” said Ted Garrish, assistant secretary for nuclear energy.
Westinghouse expects several hundred contractors to work on the project at its peak, alongside an internal team of approximately 30 to 50 people. The company says the construction will create opportunities for local contractors, subcontractors and suppliers.
Some of the new manufacturing technology will require additional technical skills. Westinghouse says it is working with local technical schools, colleges, and universities to help prepare employees for that work.

items.title: Why the WMS Must Evolve Beyond the Four Walls of the Warehouse
items.description: The warehouse can no longer operate as an isolated node. Instead, the solution is a symbiotic relationship, with systems so integrated issues are identified and dealt with as early in the process.
items.excerpt:
It’s a time of expansion, and today’s supply chain lives in unprecedented times. The post-pandemic world continues to be reshaped daily by conflict, political machinations, and a more connected than ever global community.
Traditionally, the supply chain ran on historical data, emphasizing the need for cheaper and linear paths. Reliance on historical data was the norm, and each individual step of the supply chain relied on the due diligence of the one before it.
But in an era with little precedence, historical data can only go so far and predict so much. With heightened geopolitical tensions, increasing consumer demands, and rising costs, this traditional system is no longer viable.
Warehouse management technology (WMT) has focused primarily on optimizing what happens inside the warehouse, but the operations of the present are being asked to respond to real-time changes in orders, inventory, transportation, suppliers, and demand.
As a result, the warehouse can no longer operate as an isolated node. Instead, the solution is a symbiotic relationship, with systems so integrated that issues are identified and dealt with as early in the process as raw material procurement.
Synergy is often a corporate buzzword used excessively in the boardroom, but in the everyday function of the supply chain, it’s an absolute necessity. Establishing data connectivity between the WMS (Warehouse Management System) with ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) and TMS (Transportation Management System) ensures the continued functioning and flourishing of the process as a whole.
The blunt truth is that it’s impossible to improve what isn’t measured, and KPI’s need to be measured from start to finish. Ensuring on-time delivery, order accuracy, and inventory turns are the basics necessary for success.
With a fully integrated system, inventory levels and order statuses are automatically put in sync, and the incorporation of financial and customer data is vital for a comprehensive review of logistics expenses. This improved visibility links what was traditionally isolated data in its own node, to a piece of a bigger and broader predictor for financial planning.
And the benefits are cascading. Integration provides automated alerts, providing continuous feedback in such facets as labor scheduling and warehouse layout. This allows for data consolidation into single interfaces, making it easier to monitor across the warehouse and transportation functions.

文章梳理了 PHP2Shell 从泄露到修复的完整时间线，指出 AI 大幅压缩漏洞发现成本，攻防节奏失衡成为新的底层矛盾。
https://x.com/i/article/2113093470856572928
首先是前天，也就是10月20日夜里11点多，Hacker News上突然冒出来一条帖子。
发帖的人自己写着，除了“信源：信我就行”（trust me, bro）之外，我没有任何证据，然后甚至还附上了漏洞编号。
但这一条，几个小时后被一家叫watchTowr的安全公司确认了。他们的原话是：“我们本来都该等到周四的。”
这一下就尴尬了，因为这个漏洞是巨大的，已经处于泄密状态了，真的有心人已经可以开始利用，但PHP官方的安全更新还在打包中，原定于22号晚上更新，可这瞬间就有两天的空档，如果这两天之内漏洞被利用且被攻破，后果不堪设想。
又过了一个多小时，PHP官方急忙发了预告：原定10月22日的安全更新，被迫提前到21日晚上10点（北京时间），尽可能的压缩时间。
一家参与发现这两个漏洞的安全公司，叫Calif，居然不小心把一段攻击演示视频发到了网上，充分的说明了，这个世界就是一个巨大的草台班子。
视频里，他们展示了如何利用这些漏洞，在多个目标上成功运行攻击验证程序，虽然视频很快就删了，但没办法，手快已经有人保存下来，开始在社区上大肆传播。
原本大家只知道有两个严重漏洞，连具体怎么攻击都不知道，现在，连攻击演示视频都有了，就差手把手教学了。
然后在各种离谱的AI加速之下，安全研究人员开始加速复现，网上各种号称能利用漏洞的代码也开始冒出来。
生死时速的16个小时，如果是以前，恶意之人，可能还没办法在这么短的时间里发起大规模的攻击，但是如今，是AI时代了，16个小时，对于用AI加速后的人们来说，好像有点太长了。
更离谱的是，21日下午3点41分，一家做容器镜像的公司，比约定时间提前了6个多小时，把已经打好补丁的镜像发了出去，PHP基金会直接开骂了：“无视了多方数周的协调工作。”
因为这年头，懂行的人拿新旧两版代码让AI直接暴力对比一下，直接就知道漏洞在哪了，用AI研究补丁，用AI逆向分析漏洞，再用AI开发攻击程序。
但大量正常网站的管理员，却还没有能够直接安装的更新包，这意味着攻击者直接开了天眼，直接抢跑。
21日这一天，荷兰的数字身份系统、议会网站，连国家网络安全中心自己的网站，挨个下线。
芬兰政府的IT服务商也关掉了一批服务，美国一家做人力资源软件的公司 BambooHR直接停服，提醒客户发薪相关业务可能受到影响，日本的 niconico和pixiv进入紧急维护。
因为日本的PHP网站实在太多了，甚至高市早苗都去X上发文，建议预防性下线，直到晚上10点的PHP更新推送。
一个编程语言的漏洞，让高市早苗半夜发推，让好几个国家的政府主动拔网线，这种画面，说实话，我真没见过。
晚上10点，PHP安全更新上线，对于这两项严重漏洞来说，没有任何完整的缓解措施，更新是唯一安全的选择。
而这个漏洞，还不是啥新模型整的，是几个月前，用GPT-5.6 Sol发现的，所以大家就可以想象，如果是这些大模型公司的未发布的内部的更强模型去扫的话，全世界的各种网络基建，那可能真的全都有问题。。。
同时，OpenAI这次也紧急发布了一个skill，来辅助你发现，你的网站是否会受到影响。
这里希望大家一定要注意，如果你自己的网站中，使用了PHP，如果你还不知道这些消息，请看到的第一时间，立刻，立刻更新版本，也希望能扩散给你的朋友。
那我觉得，要理解这次为什么闹这么大，全球反应为啥这么过度，得先知道PHP是个什么东西。
首先，我们可能都知道，你在浏览器里点开一个网页，服务器那边得现场算出来这一页该显示什么，比如你是谁，购物车里有什么，这篇文章下面有几条评论等等，那干这个活的程序，叫后端。
不过因为太老了，现在很多公司的新产品或者新技术栈都不太用了，并且有意思的是，PHP在程序员圈子里一直是被嘲的对象，“PHP是世界上最好的语言”，当了十几年的梗，很多人都觉得它是上个世纪的东西。
但在全球，用PHP搭的网站，依然占据着70%，即使是新一点的国内，虽然Java极多，以2026年10月的数据看，依然还有超过一半的网站，是用PHP搭的。
你注册过的论坛、小店的付款页、很多地方政府的办事网站、公司内部的报销系统，还有路由器和NAS的管理后台，大概率都有一个跑在PHP上的。
这次的漏洞有个名字，叫PHP2Shell。Shell就是服务器的命令行，拿到它，你就可以认为约等于拿到了这台服务器的控制权了，所以这个名字的意思极其直接，从PHP，直通你的服务器。
严重程度用 CVSS 打分，满分10分，最开始泄露版本是满分，但是最后其实给的是9.2分。
就是程序跑起来的时候，要不停地向系统“借”内存，用来存放临时数据，然后用完再“还”回去，PHP的解释器是用C语言写的，C语言跑得快，但借和还，依然全靠程序员自己记账，系统可不管你。
第一个漏洞，CVE-2026-109619，专业名词叫“释放后使用”（use-after-free）。
举个例子，你开了一家酒店，第一个客人来寄存行李，服务员把他的东西放进了18号柜子，并且在本子上记了下来。
第二个人刚把自己的东西放进去，服务员就拿着旧记录，跑去打开18号柜子，还以为里面是第一个人的行李。
PHP这次的问题，就出在类似的地方，原本已经归还的内存，又被拿去存放新的数据，但PHP还留着指向原来位置的旧记录。
于是，它以为自己在处理上一份数据，实际上碰到的早就成了另一份数据，所以，如果攻击者能精心操纵这个过程，就有机会读取、篡改原本不该碰

据雅虎财经援引知情人士报道，Anthropic 最早或于本周五公开提交 S-1 招股说明书，推进有望创史上最大规模的 IPO。
转载自雅虎财经的上市进展报道，给出了招股书时间线、营收亏损数字和估值预期，可帮助读者了解 AI 公司上市节奏。
IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，当地时间 21 日，据雅虎财经援引三名知情人士消息称，Anthropic 最早或于本周五公开提交 S-1 招股说明书，为有望创下史上最大规模的 IPO 迈出关键一步。
Anthropic 的上市计划备受关注，预计规模将超过 SpaceX 今年 6 月的 IPO 。随着投资者对 AI 行业巨额支出的担忧加剧，市场普遍认为，Anthropic 上市将成为检验投资者对 AI 热潮还有多大兴趣的一次重要考验。
今年 6 月，Anthropic 向美国证券交易委员会秘密提交了 IPO 申请草案。根据规定，采用保密申报程序的企业，须在正式投资者路演开始至少 15 个自然日前公开申请文件。
如果顺利公开招股书，Anthropic 距离 11 月上市 就将更近一步，但最终发行时间仍受市场环境等因素影响。届时，普通投资者也将首次得以了解其具体财务数据及潜在风险。
Anthropic 斥资数十亿美元建设 AI 基础设施，以支持 Claude 系列模型的训练和运行。除了与谷歌、亚马逊合作，公司还租用 SpaceX 旗下 Colossus 1 数据中心的 GPU 算力。
今年上半年，Anthropic 营收达到 163 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,090.36 亿元人民币） ，净亏损超过 800 亿美元 （现汇率约合 5,351.46 亿元人民币） 。华尔街预计 Anthropic 可能通过 IPO 募资最多 1,000 亿美元 （现汇率约合 6,689.33 亿元人民币） ，对应估值高达 2 万亿美元 （现汇率约合 13.38 万亿元人民币） 。
另有消息称，Anthropic 上周在旧金山办公室向投资者透露，第三季度营收达到 168 亿美元 （现汇率约合 1,123.81 亿元人民币） ，高于第二季度的 115 亿美元 （现汇率约合 769.27 亿元人民币） 。按调整后口径计算，公司也实现了盈利。
一名知情人士称，Anthropic 的上市规模如此庞大，选择何时启动 IPO，也将对未来几周准备上市的其他企业产生重要影响。
竞争对手 OpenAI 原本预计今年启动 IPO，目前则预计于 2027 年初上市。

items.excerpt:
Running a small or medium-sized trucking fleet means balancing safety, operating costs, driver performance, and customer expectations every day.
In-cab safety solutions such as cameras can help carriers gain better visibility into what happens on the road while giving fleet managers useful information to improve safety and protect their business.
For many smaller fleets, investing in new technology can seem like an unnecessary expense. Fleet managers may assume that advanced camera systems are designed primarily for large carriers with hundreds of trucks.
In reality, smaller fleets can benefit significantly from an AI dash cam because every vehicle, driver, and incident can have a meaningful impact on the business.
Fleet managers cannot be inside every truck at the same time. GPS tracking can show where a vehicle is, while telematics can provide information about speed, location, and vehicle activity. Cameras add another important layer: visual context.
A camera can help fleet managers understand what actually happened during a driving event. This can be especially valuable after a collision, sudden braking event, traffic violation, or customer complaint.
Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) research has also examined onboard monitoring systems that combine video and vehicle-performance data to provide feedback on risky driving behavior. The goal is to give drivers and safety managers more targeted information they can use to improve driving performance.
For smaller fleets, this visibility can help turn safety management from a reactive process into a more proactive one.
Driver training does not have to end after orientation. Effective fleets continuously reinforce safe driving habits, and video can make that process more practical.

Ahead of this year's Pack Expo International show, which takes place Oct. 18 to 21 in Chicago, we asked several of the leading players in this diverse industry about developments in their part of this world and the outlook for the future. Here's what they had to say.
Q: HOW WOULD YOU DESCRIBE THE CURRENT STATE OF THE PACKAGING AUTOMATION INDUSTRY?
William Nelson – E80: The industry is moving very quickly from stand-alone automation toward fully integrated systems. For years, manufacturers often automated one process at a time: a palletizer here, a wrapper there, an AGV [automated guided vehicle] fleet somewhere else. Today, particularly in the CPG [consumer packaged goods] industry, companies are looking at the entire material flow and asking how all those operations can work together as one system.
This is why we are seeing more customers look for long-term technology partners rather than individual equipment suppliers. The conversation increasingly starts with the overall process: What does the plant or distribution center need to accomplish today, what will it need to accomplish five or 10 years from now, and how can automation provide the flexibility and scalability to support that growth?
J Welch – Regal Rexnord: Packaging automation continues to evolve as manufacturers adapt to e-commerce growth, faster fulfillment expectations, and more dynamic product portfolios. As a result, companies are prioritizing flexible, scalable automation that can quickly accommodate changing packaging formats, production demands, and distribution models.
Q: WHAT MAJOR INNOVATIONS IN PACKAGING AUTOMATION HAVE YOU SEEN IN RECENT YEARS?
J Welch – Regal Rexnord: Right-size packaging systems and shuttle-based AS/RS [automated storage and retrieval system] solutions have transformed how manufacturers optimize packaging, warehouse space, and fulfillment efficiency. At the same time, increased automation adoption has heightened the need for integrated systems that seamlessly connect material handling, packaging, and warehouse operations.

Transportation management systems were originally built to price, execute, and track shipments. Now users are asking for features to help them deal with everything from legal turmoil and diesel price spikes to the recent surge in cargo theft.
Ben Ames has spent 30 years as a journalist since starting out as a reporter for daily newspapers in Pennsylvania and Massachusetts. He has focused on business and technology reporting since 1999 for trade journals including Cahners’ Design News and Modern Materials Handling magazines, and other magazines with PennWell and IDG. A native New Yorker, Ames went to college in Maine and now lives with his family outside of Boston, where they all love to hike and kayak.
Transportation management system (TMS) software has been a mainstay of logistics operations for years, helping users plan and arrange for the physical transport of goods across the supply chain while striking the optimal balance between cost and speed.
For decades, the software has paid for itself by generating savings and efficiencies in straightforward freight hauls. But the events of recent months have injected unprecedented levels of uncertainty into the business of cargo transport—whether by truck, rail, ocean, or air. Instead of simply arranging for cargo to be hauled from point A to point B, companies now have to worry about major variables that can change from day to day, including radical swings in diesel fuel prices caused by geopolitical conflict, attacks on containerships and sudden closures of ocean lanes, soaring rates of cargo theft, and unexpected court rulings that place new legal burdens on businesses.
"For most of the last two decades, a TMS existed to execute a shipment, price it, and track it through delivery. That was the job. Today, the same platform is being asked to absorb a much wider set of forces at once: legal and security risk, cost volatility, and global disruption, often in the same week," says Raddy Velkov, senior vice president of carrier sales and strategy at BlueGrace Logistics , a Florida-based third-party logistics service provider (3PL). "None of those four pressures existed at this intensity five years ago. Now a platform has to account for all of them at once, and that's a meaningfully bigger job than the one TMS platforms were originally built to do."

items.title: Why Hardware Specialization is Back
items.description: Thirty years ago, general-purpose chips beat specialized ones in the semiconductor industry’s great strategy debate. Today the same debate is back, but with new constraints.
items.excerpt:
In 1990, Eugene Brooks of Lawrence Livermore told the Supercomputing conference that nothing would withstand the attack of the killer micros. “Micro” referred to microprocessor, meaning a general-purpose chip that did a good job at most types of computation. They were also being sold by the millions per year into desktop PCs, delivering faster and faster performance each year.
Around that same time, competing specialized architectures, such as vector processors, massively parallel processors (MPPs), and Lisp machines started dying off en masse. ETA systems closed in 1989, Multiflow in 1990, Alliant in 1992, Symbolics in 1993, Kendall Square Research and Thinking Machines (not the same one as today) in 1994, and Cray Computer in 1995. Danny Hillis, the founder of Thinking Machines, remarked years later that “… ultimately these things were just going to be boxes of microprocessors.”
Interestingly, these specialized chips didn’t lose because they were superior at unimportant problems. The general-purpose microprocessor was actually outperforming them, not just on a wide spectrum of workloads, but on the very workloads the specialized chips were designed for.
And although the companies that made them didn’t make it, the ideas they brought lived on inside other chips. CPUs absorbed vector processing as SSE and AVX, and massively parallel designs influenced both multi-core CPU and GPU architectures. The pattern at the time was that the specialists came up with good ideas, but the generalist chips absorbed those ideas into a single architecture.
Today, we are in the middle of another heyday for the industry. AI workloads are different enough from traditional software workloads that the industry is in the midst of rethinking what computing should actually look like, with many different new chips and ideas behind them.
There is a massive explosion of new accelerators to serve AI workloads, and GPUs generate more revenue for chip companies than CPUs do (although CPUs are also in their own demand crunch right now). In times like this, it’s interesting to look back on the last hardware boom and see what has changed since last time (and what remains the same), to better predict what will happen next. Is this time different for specialized chips, or will they ultimately be absorbed into general purpose chips like before?

items.excerpt:
Report tracks shifting distribution networks as inland markets capture their highest share of U.S. industrial net real estate absorption since 2010.
Despite strong U.S. container import volumes, warehouse vacancy rates near seaports rose 20 basis points to 7.7% through July, up from year-end 2025 and above the national rate of 6.8%, according to Cushman & Wakefield.
The reasons for the empty warehouse space include shifting distribution networks and an oversupply of new warehouse supply, the commercial real estate firm said in a report titled “From Port to Property: Resilient Import Volumes Amid Shifting Trade Patterns and Industrial Demand.”
The drop-off in rental rates came as imports at 10 major U.S. maritime ports increased 0.5% year over year through July, exceeding 14.5 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs). And monthly imported container volumes exceeded 2 million TEUs in May, June and July.
But instead of renting inventory storage space at ports, companies have been storing their goods elsewhere. In fact, inland markets captured 83% of U.S. industrial net absorption in the first half of 2026, their highest share since 2010.
Inland markets have attracted occupiers because they offer lower labor, rent, and energy costs than port markets, the report said. In addition, growing imports from Mexico have supported demand for distribution facilities served directly by truck and rail, without goods first passing through a U.S. maritime port.
“Cargo volumes tell only part of the warehouse demand story,” said Jason Price, Head of Americas Logistics & Industrial Research at Cushman & Wakefield. “Goods continue to arrive, but where companies choose to store and distribute them is changing. Inland markets offer cost advantages, while imports arriving through Mexico can move directly into inland distribution networks. At the same time, port markets are still absorbing space delivered during the construction boom.”
Despite the overall improving leasing activity, risks remain, the report warned. Inflation, elevated interest rates, and rising energy prices could constrain consumer spending and occupier demand, while further changes in trade policy could alter cargo flows and distribution decisions.

items.excerpt:
Intramotev will build TugVolt autonomous railcars for $16.2 million federal project.
Autonomous freight railcar builder Intramotev this week said it will provide its technology for a federally funded project to run robotic locomotives on Missouri’s Columbia Terminal Railroad (COLT).
Specifically, Saint Louis, Missouri-based Intramotev will serve as the technology partner on a $16.2 million federal grant. The Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) announced this week that it has selected the City of Columbia for a grant under its Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) program.
Intramotev will deploy two TugVolt autonomous railcars on COLT’s 21.4-mile line between Centralia and Columbia, Missouri. Operations will advance in phases under an FRA-approved test program. They begin with remote switching at COLT’s Columbia terminal and build to autonomous freight service across the full mainline and its public crossings.
The project’s goal is to produce a safety record that FRA and the more than 600 U.S. short lines can use as a template for adopting autonomous railcars.
“Short lines keep America’s small cities and rural communities connected to the freight network. Autonomous railcars can help them serve more customers, more often, at lower cost, and this program will show what that looks like on a working mainline. We’re proud to partner with the City of Columbia and COLT, and grateful to FRA for its support of this important milestone for the rail industry,” said Tim Luchini, Intramotev’s CEO.

items.excerpt:
Deal with German certification group TUV SUD will streamline safety certification process for physical AI technologies.
Accenture will collaborate with a German certification organization to accelerate the installation of physical AI platforms in automated factories and warehouses , the consulting firm said today.
By working with TUV SUD, which is a testing, inspection, and certification organization , Accenture said it can now help companies safely deploy physical AI equipment such as autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) alongside human workers faster. Specifically, the partners’ “Physical AI Safety Suite” will allow clients to navigate the intricate web of standards for adopting physical AI-enabled automation solutions.
Established industry standards are important because they provide the basis for ensuring that automated facilities are designed and operated safely. An example is ISO 3691-4, which specifies safety requirements for driverless industrial trucks and systems, including AMRs. But such a process can take several weeks for a medium-sized production plant to follow the standard process of iterative coordination, validation, and acceptance of safety concepts.
Now, the Physical AI Safety Suite partially digitizes the manual assessment of facilities, equipment, and preparation of certification packages, using digital twins and AI-powered simulations. TÜV SÜD estimates that the digital process could bring production online up to 30% sooner.
“Physical AI enables robotic systems to become increasingly adaptive while also paving the way for an independent, evidence-based digital certification process,” said Patrick Vollmer, CEO and Chairman of the Board at TÜV SÜD AG. “Through our Physical AI Safety Suite, which leverages simulation-generated evidence, we can support compliance-readiness much earlier in the engineering lifecycle without compromising the rigor safety standards require. Assessing automation concepts before the first robot is deployed reduces uncertainty in live operations and helps drive higher levels of safety, efficiency and performance across production and logistics.”
Accenture defines physical AI as a mix of technologies, including digital twins, simulations, sensors, robots and AI models, which enables robots and machines to sense, decide, act and improve constantly under changing conditions and operate more autonomously in real environments. items.excerpt:
System allows heavy-duty trucks to be refueled in about eight minutes for a range of up to 450 miles.
Toyota Motor North America says it has installed two mobile hydrogen fueling devices at its largest parts distribution facility in the U.S., allowing heavy-duty trucks to be refueled in about eight minutes for a range of up to 450 miles.
With the tanks and fuel ready, Toyota's commercial logistics fleets plan to use the mobile fuelers to support Toyota operations by fueling heavy-duty fuel cell trucks hauling freight from the Port of Los Angeles to Ontario, and throughout the region. A permanent station is planned to be built at the location, which Toyota calls its North American Parts Center California (NAPCC).
The station will initially fuel heavy-duty trucks commissioned through Hyroad Energy and will later integrate heavy-duty trucks with Toyota's own certified fuel cell powertrain. Production Toyota-powered trucks are expected to hit the open road for commercial operations in 2027.
In a public-private partnership, Toyota is collaborating with the U.S. Department of Energy's National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) in Golden, Colorado, to research several initiatives, including 70 MPa high-flow hydrogen fueling for heavy-duty trucks.
High-flow fueling allows trucks to accept hydrogen fuel at speeds up to 300g/s, or about five times faster than the rate of conventional light-duty fueling technology. It allows heavy-duty trucks to carry energy into the vehicle at an equivalent speed of a 20 MW fast charger. Refueling times are comparable to modern diesel-powered, heavy-duty trucks. Unlike a diesel powertrain, however, fuel cells emit only water.
The company supports the research through its Toyota Hydrogen Headquarters (H2HQ) division , which is the lead office in North America for the development, engineering, commercialization, and business operations of Toyota's hydrogen fuel cell technologies. Based in Gardena, California, H2HQ works collaboratively with Toyota's R&D offices in Michigan and Texas, as well as business units in Japan and internationally, to create zero-emissions fuel cell technologies that enable energy independence, innovation, and the movement of people, goods, energy, and information.

items.excerpt:
Overhaul finds 34% increase in the theft of data center equipment, chips, and computing components since 2024.
The artificial intelligence arms race has created a new target for cargo thieves, who have stolen more than $150 million in AI equipment this year, according to supply chain visibility provider Overhaul.
Overhaul’s AI Infrastructure Intel Report also found a 34% increase in the theft of data center equipment, chips, and computing components since 2024.
The methods thieves use to steal equipment are also changing from force to fraud, shaping what shippers need to watch for to stay vigilant. Overhaul’s report shows that deception was used to steal 92% of high-value technology shipments. Thieves used methods such as fraudulent carrier identities, double-brokering, spoofed communications, and falsified paperwork to slip inside legitimate freight transactions and steal loads.
According to Overhaul, a single flagship AI server rack costs roughly $3 million, so one truckload routinely carries eight figures of value, and all of it moves on ordinary roads before it is installed. Overhaul found that individual losses now regularly exceed $30 million, with such thefts occurring weekly.
“AI hardware is some of the most concentrated value moving through the supply chain right now, and it’s become the fastest-growing target for these criminal networks,” said Barry Conlon, CEO and Founder of Overhaul. “As thieves become increasingly deceptive, visibility into a shipment alone isn’t enough to stop it from being taken. Our findings give shippers the intelligence to know how crews take loads, where the equipment ends up, and what to put in place now so they can stop the next theft before it happens.”

items.excerpt:
Today's PHP Security Release, and How We're Strengthening PHP Security ( via ) If you're running anything on PHP it's vital you upgrade - today's updates (across the entire PHP 8.x line) address two remote code execution holes, and there have been exploits circulating since last night, thanks to a leak in the coordinated disclosure process.
This post from the PHP Foundation explain what went so wrong:
On Tuesday, October 20th, at around 15:00 UTC, the two CVE IDs began circulating on online forums and social media. They came with a wrong release time and a wrong CVSS score of 10.0 (the actual score is 9.2). No technical details leaked. In response, the PHP project brought its pre-announcement forward and published it at 19:30 UTC . It also moved the release from October 22nd, 14:00 UTC, to October 21st, 14:00 UTC [...]
As a result of the leak and pre-announcement around 20:00 UTC, Calif, one of the security firms that had reported the issues mistakenly published a video. It showed their proof of concept working against a number of targets and revealed a few additional, though limited, details about the vulnerabilities. Copies of the deleted video started circulating on social media soon after. The video contributed to accelerated development of various PoCs (exploitation proof of concepts), which then increased circulation on October 21st.

items.title: NVIDIA Kumo Relational Outperforms Supervised Machine Learning on Relational Data, No Training Required
items.excerpt:
NVIDIA Kumo Relational is a pre-trained relational foundation model that makes predictions directly on enterprise databases. Given a predictive query, it gathers up to 10,000 historical examples as context and predicts outcomes such as churn, demand, or fraud in a single forward pass. It needs no task-specific training, no feature engineering, and no flattening of tables. Kumo Relational is the first few-shot foundation model to outperform supervised machine learning on common relational benchmarks. Across 41 tasks on 15 databases, it beats supervised relational deep learning models and expert-engineered gradient-boosted tree pipelines, and on the SAP SALT enterprise benchmark it surpasses AutoGluon ensembles by 8% in mean reciprocal rank (MRR). It scales to databases with 500B+ rows and works for humans and agents alike, through NVIDIA's open-source, GPU-native structured-data-models library or as an NVIDIA NIM.
Foundation models have already rewritten the playbook for language and vision. Not long ago, production NLP meant a dedicated model per task, each fed by its own pipeline of tokenization, lemmatization, and n-grams. LLMs made that stack largely obsolete for three reasons: they were more accurate than the best task-specific models, far simpler to put into production, and flexible enough to open a new era of agentic applications.
The same shift is now underway for structured data. Relational databases power the world's most critical business decisions, yet predictive modeling on them still requires weeks of feature engineering, task-specific training, and tuned pipelines. Structured data foundation models change that for the same three reasons:
Better accuracy today: As drop-in replacements, these models already beat many production pipelines, especially XGBoost. On RelBench V1 classification tasks, Kumo Relational outperforms gradient-boosted trees on expert-engineered features by nearly 4 AUROC points on average. On SAP SALT, it beats XGBoost on engineered features by 7 MRR points out of the box and by 13 MRR points after fine-tuning. These results make a compelling case for replacing production XGBoost pipelines with Kumo Relational.
Simplicity and agility: One pre-trained model replaces separate pipelines for individual tasks. A new prediction becomes a query instead of a project, so ML teams can finally take on use cases that traditional ML made too laborious to build at every level of the organization.

items.description: AI 安全公司 Calif 用 GPT-5.6 Sol 在 PHP 中发现两个 CVSS 9.2 严重漏洞，可让无账号攻击者接管 Web 服务器，影响远至 PHP 5.4 的版本，PHP 提前一天紧急发布修复。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/heuaxyy5ixq9x5wtoobw5wq7e
items.excerpt:
AI 安全公司 Calif 用 GPT-5.6 Sol 在 PHP 中发现两个 CVSS 9.2 严重漏洞，可让无账号攻击者接管 Web 服务器，影响远至 PHP 5.4 的版本，PHP 提前一天紧急发布修复。
原文梳理了 AI 发现 PHP 严重漏洞的细节与修复过程，并附上可复用的 PHP 版本检查 Codex skill 入口。
使用 GPT-5.6 Sol 的研究人员在 PHP 中发现了一个极其严重的漏洞，PHP 驱动着约 70% 的网站，该漏洞导致主要网站下线，运营方纷纷紧急修补。
发现该漏洞的 AI 安全公司 Calif 在一份声明中表示，如果不尽快修补，这些漏洞可能使全球 70% 的网站面临风险，并称其为“AI 发现的最严重漏洞，甚至可能是整个软件史上最严重的漏洞”。
PHP 紧急发布了修复程序，因为这些漏洞可能让无账号的攻击者接管 Web 服务器。
两个漏洞在 CVSS 严重性评分中均为 9.2 分，影响低至 5.4 的 PHP 版本。
当请求在错误的时机触及 PHP 的内存上限时，PHP 会释放内存但保留指向该内存的指针，该工作进程上后续的请求便可劫持这块内存。
审计人员在 2024 年发现了这一弱点，但修复工作停滞了数月，部分原因是没有人展示过实际攻击。
现由 Google 拥有的云安全公司 Wiz 表示，这些模型让一名研究人员在一周内完成了过去顶尖团队需要数月才能完成的工作。
CVE 编号的泄露迫使 PHP 提前一天发布，Cloudflare 目前报告称已出现早期攻击尝试。

items.title: How Specializing the Vocabulary of SLMs Can Cut Inference Cost by 77% in Real Applications
items.excerpt:
Models specialized for a domain or a task by fine-tuning general open-source models, such as Qwen and Gemma, inherit a vocabulary built for many domains and general applications.
In an essay grader we run in production, that vocabulary split the text the model writes most into many tokens. This article previews some results from the VocabX paper, which we will publish soon: how we specialized the vocabulary around the cost of each token rather than its frequency, and cut measured inference cost by 77% without changing the base model.
The tokenizer is usually treated as a fixed property of the base model, inherited and left alone. For a model specialized in a single domain, it can be one of the largest cost levers, and it is set before any training step.
One of the systems we run in production is an automated grader for Portuguese essays, built on Qwen3-4B. It receives the essay, the prompt and the supporting texts, and returns a JSON assessment with a grade and a comment for each competency.
The model was already small, at 4 billion parameters, and had already been trained for the task. Its tokenizer, however, was still the original Qwen3-4B one, built for many languages and many kinds of text. In the grader, it was used for a single language, Portuguese, and a single response format. That had two costs: the text the grader writes on every request took more tokens than it needed, and at every generated token the model scored a vocabulary of 151,669 entries, including many this task almost never uses.
We rebuilt that vocabulary with a method we call VocabX, keeping the same base model, the same data and the same training recipe. The numbers in this article come from the current version of the paper, still under review, and may change before publication.
The leading language models read and write in tokens, and the tokenizer decides how text becomes tokens. The tokenizers of the leading general-purpose models are trained on large collections of text from many domains and languages, from source code to contracts to Chinese. For a general-purpose model, that choice makes sense.
For a model used in a single domain, it creates two kinds of waste at once.
The first is fragmentation. The tokenizer splits into many pieces exactly what the domain repeats most. In the grader, every response starts with the same JSON envelope, the same competency names, the same evaluation phrases. In contracts, it is the boilerplate clauses. In code, the identifiers. items.title: Where TMS Fits in the New Architecture of Logistics
items.description: Where TMS Fits in the New Architecture of Logistics is fundamentally an architecture question. The category does not create value in isolation; it creates value through the interfaces between data, decisions, physical operations, people, and adjacent execution systems. The post Where TMS Fits in the New Architecture of Logistics appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
TMS creates value as part of a larger operating architecture, not in isolation. Its role is defined by the interfaces among data, decisions, physical operations, people, carriers, and adjacent execution systems.
At its core, the freight-centric planning and execution system used to translate orders and demand into feasible transportation plans, carrier decisions, tenders, shipment execution, visibility, settlement, and performance management. Around it sits an architecture where ERP and OMS supply demand and order context; TMS converts that context into freight plans and execution; carrier networks, visibility, telematics, WMS/YMS, parcel, payment, and decision layers continuously update the operating state. The design challenge is to preserve clear accountability while allowing operating state and decisions to move across those boundaries. The position of TMS in the new architecture follows from Transportation Is Becoming Computational , where optimization, events, carrier interaction, and execution become part of a continuously updated decision process.
A connected architecture does not require every system to store the same data or one suite to own every transaction. It requires the systems involved in a decision to share enough trusted state, at the right latency, for the combined operation to respond coherently.
That becomes visible in cases such as a tender rejection, a late pickup, a new order after the plan is built, a capacity shortfall, a missed delivery window, or a warehouse constraint that makes the transportation plan infeasible. The local system may be functioning correctly while the end-to-end outcome is deteriorating. Architecture determines whether that mismatch can be recognized and corrected before the intervention window closes.
TMS is moving from periodic planning and transaction execution toward continuous transportation management, where plans are refreshed as orders, capacity, service risk, and operating constraints change This does not erase the category boundary. The category remains freight-centric, but the boundary is expanding as TMS providers add visibility, dynamic replanning, exception workflows, procurement, analytics, AI, and network services It does mean buyers should evaluate the connections between systems as part of the functional solution, not as integration work to be solved after selection.

A manufacturing security awareness program has to reach people whose working days look very different. A design engineer reviewing drawings, a buyer approving a supplier change and a production supervisor arranging maintenance may encounter different requests and use different devices.
Giving all three the same lesson can leave the most important decision in each person’s workflow unexplained.
The platforms below are compared using public product capabilities and their fit for employee learning, rather than hands-on benchmarks. They address awareness, phishing practice and related program administration.
They should be evaluated as part of an employee security program; choosing one does not provide industrial network monitoring, machine protection or an operational technology security architecture.
Map how each employee group will access training before comparing content libraries. Consider shared workstations, language preferences, accessibility needs and whether a person routinely has an individual inbox.
Define practical scenarios with operations leaders: an unexpected remote-support request, an altered purchase instruction or a supplier file that asks for unusual access. Keep exercises away from production systems and schedule learning around agreed work windows.
The evaluation should show that employees can reach the material, understand the expected action and find the correct escalation route. Completion reporting is useful, but it should sit beside evidence that the instruction makes sense in the role.

Its explicit manufacturing context makes it worth examining with representatives from the factory and engineering office. Select a few lessons and ask employees to explain how the examples relate to their actual work.
Review whether the reporting route named in the lesson matches the one staff can use on shift. A buyer should also verify delivery arrangements for employees without individual mailboxes and decide how managers will provide time for learning without turning completion into a last-minute administrative exercise.
